caption:
Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for its latest quarter, up 103% from a year ago and well above Wall Street's forecast.
It is the company's first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. Interim CEO Colette Kress now leads it.
Nvidia expects about $130 billion next quarter, without counting on China.

Does Nvidia even need Jensen Huang back?

paragraphs.text: Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for its third quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended October 25, 2026, in results released after the market closed on November 17, 2026. Revenue rose 20% from the previous quarter and 103% from a year earlier, the company said.

The results came in above Wall Street's expectations. According to TipRanks, analysts had expected revenue of about $108.97 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.48 a share. Nvidia reported adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share, and TipRanks reported that the shares rose in after-hours trading.

Data center revenue reached $107.6 billion, up 21% from the prior quarter and 110% from a year earlier. Nvidia now reports its remaining business as Edge Computing, which brought in $8.2 billion. GAAP net income was $65.3 billion and GAAP gross margin was 74.8%. The company returned $28.1 billion to shareholders during the quarter and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.25 per share, payable December 23, 2026.

In the release, Nvidia said its Vera Rubin NVL72 systems had entered production and begun shipping, calling it the fastest product ramp in its history. It listed CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius among the companies running Vera Rubin racks, and it repeated that it has agreed to acquire Hugging Face.

The quarter is the first Nvidia has reported since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. Colette Kress, the company's chief financial officer since 2013, took over as interim CEO on November 12, 2026, according to TheStreet and The Next Web. The release quotes Kress, not Huang, who said the company's momentum is real.

The report arrived during a steep slide in the stock. The Next Web reported that Nvidia shares closed at $156.14 on November 16 after falling 4%, had lost about 35% since their all-time high in October and had fallen for six straight weeks. Options traders had priced in a move of about 7% in either direction after the report.

Nvidia forecast fourth quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, with gross margins of 71% to 72%. The quarter includes an extra week. The company said the outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China. TipRanks put the analyst consensus for the quarter at $124.9 billion.

Before the report, analysts had raised questions about how much of Nvidia's Southeast Asian sales ultimately serve Chinese companies. The Next Web cited a UBS estimate that, in a worst case, new scrutiny of sales into Singapore and Malaysia could cut up to about 10% of revenue.

The numbers suggest demand for Nvidia's chips has not been shaken by the leadership crisis or the stock's decline. Whether investors return depends less on this quarter than on who runs the company next and how much of its overseas business holds up under the new export scrutiny.
Watch the earnings call commentary from Kress and the board's next step on a permanent CEO, including whether Huang returns.
